(i) the redacted images are not completely purged of the sensitive information, (ii) the residual information is hidden in the artifacts of the compression process and (iii) the residual information may be exploited to identify the correct template with high certainty.
the compression artifacts in redacted images can be exploited to reveal information about the original images.
the residual information of redacted images can be hidden in the compression artifacts and can be exploited when a redacted image has low entropy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
redacting images with simple methods can be ineffective in hiding information.
, if the original and the redacted images are compressed in the same bit rate, then the redacted images can be effectively purged from any information of the original.
the residual information in the redacted image is sufficient to identify the original if the image has low entropy, and the compression scheme and the bit rate are carefully chosen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the compression scheme and the redaction method must be carefully chosen when disseminating sensitive images.
the compression of redacted images should be done at the same quality as that of the original.
, even when a simple method is used to remove sensitive information from images, residual information might still be present.
